## Setup

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)
```

# Part I: Paired data

```{r}
zinc <- tibble(
  location = 1:10,
  bottom = c(
    0.430, 0.266, 0.567, 0.531, 0.707,
    0.716, 0.651, 0.589, 0.469, 0.723
  ),
  surface = c(
    0.415, 0.238, 0.390, 0.410, 0.605,
    0.609, 0.632, 0.523, 0.411, 0.612
  )
)

zinc <- zinc |>
  mutate(diff = bottom - surface)
```

```{r}
zinc |>
  summarise(
    mean_difference = mean(diff),
    sd_difference = sd(diff),
    n = n()
  )
```

```{r}
t.test(
  zinc$bottom,
  zinc$surface,
  paired = TRUE
)
```

# Part II: American salaries

```{r}
load(url(
  "https://github.com/GarciaRios/govt_3990/raw/gh-pages/Labs/lab6/acs.RData"
))

glimpse(acs)
```

```{r}
acs |>
  count(employment) |>
  mutate(
    percent = 100 * n / sum(n)
  )
```

5. What percentage of the sample is employed?

> 

```{r}
acs_emp <- acs |>
  filter(employment == "employed")
```

## Gender and income

```{r}
ggplot(
  acs_emp,
  aes(x = gender, y = income)
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
acs_emp |>
  group_by(gender) |>
  summarise(
    mean_income = mean(income, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_income = sd(income, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(income))
  )
```

6. How do average incomes differ across the two groups?

> 

7. What does the boxplot show that the means alone do not?

> 

```{r}
income_gender_test <- t.test(
  income ~ gender,
  data = acs_emp,
  alternative = "two.sided",
  conf.level = 0.95
)

income_gender_test
```

8. State \(H_0\) and \(H_A\).

> 

9. Report the p-value and 95% confidence interval.

> 

10. Interpret the population difference in context.

> 

11. What does this analysis not establish?

> 

# Part III: Could hours worked matter?

```{r}
acs_emp <- acs_emp |>
  mutate(
    emp_type = case_when(
      hrs_work >= 40 ~ "full time",
      TRUE ~ "part time"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
acs_emp |>
  count(gender, emp_type) |>
  group_by(gender) |>
  mutate(
    percent = 100 * n / sum(n)
  )
```

12. Are the gender groups equally distributed across full-time and part-time work?

> 

```{r}
acs_full <- acs_emp |>
  filter(emp_type == "full time")

acs_part <- acs_emp |>
  filter(emp_type == "part time")
```

### Full-time workers

```{r}
acs_full |>
  group_by(gender) |>
  summarise(
    mean_income = mean(income, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_income = sd(income, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(income))
  )
```

```{r}
t.test(
  income ~ gender,
  data = acs_full
)
```

### Part-time workers

```{r}
acs_part |>
  group_by(gender) |>
  summarise(
    mean_income = mean(income, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_income = sd(income, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(income))
  )
```

```{r}
t.test(
  income ~ gender,
  data = acs_part
)
```

13. Does the income difference remain among full-time workers?

14. Does it remain among part-time workers?

# Part IV: More than two groups

```{r}
acs_emp |>
  count(edu)
```

```{r}
acs_emp |>
  group_by(edu) |>
  summarise(
    mean_income = mean(income, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_income = sd(income, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(income))
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  acs_emp,
  aes(x = edu, y = income)
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal()
```

16. How many population means are being compared?

> 

17. Why would separate t-tests be a poor first approach?

> 

```{r}
income_edu_model <- aov(
  income ~ edu,
  data = acs_emp
)

summary(income_edu_model)
```

18. What is the overall ANOVA p-value?

> 

19. At \(\alpha=0.05\), reject or fail to reject \(H_0\).

> 

20. What can you conclude from the ANOVA?

> 

21. What can you not yet conclude?

> 

```{r}
TukeyHSD(income_edu_model)
```

```{r}
res <- TukeyHSD(income_edu_model)

df_tukey <- res$edu |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::as_tibble(rownames = "comparison")

ggplot(
  df_tukey,
  aes(
    x = reorder(comparison, diff),
    y = diff,
    ymin = lwr,
    ymax = upr
  )
) +
  geom_pointrange(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Difference in mean income ($)",
    title = "Pairwise differences in mean income",
    subtitle = "Tukey-adjusted 95% confidence intervals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
